Audience: first-time Connecticut applicants preparing in English for the Class D knowledge test; this section matters to every novice learning car control and to all drivers sharing roads with walkers, riders and trucks.
Level: plain-English reading level; no prior driving vocabulary is assumed, so each manual term is defined where it first appears.
Prerequisites: the licensing path of chapter one; this section opens chapter three.
Section scope: manual chapter three, first part: starting, accelerating, steering and scanning, intersections, rail crossings, work zones, vulnerable users, emergency vehicles, pedestrians, bicyclists, motorcycles, slow vehicles and trucks.
Out of scope: space management, passing and turning detail, hazardous conditions, alcohol and drug law, signs and signals, and anything not printed on the selected manual pages.
